name: YLFW
description: Face recognition has achieved outstanding performance in the last decade with the development of deep learning techniques. Nowadays, the challenges in face recognition are related to specific scenarios, for instance, the performance under diverse image quality, the robustness for aging and edge cases of person age (children and elders), distinguishing of related identities. In this set of problems, recognizing children's faces is one of the most sensitive and important. One of the reasons for this problem is the existing bias towards adults in existing face datasets. In this work, we present a benchmark dataset for children's face recognition, which is compiled similarly to the famous face recognition benchmarks LFW, CALFW, CPLFW, XQLFW and AgeDB. We also present a development dataset (separated into train and test parts) for adapting face recognition models for face images of children. reputation: A niche but useful benchmark for child face recognition that extends the LFW-style evaluation family and is mainly used in academic face-recognition research.
notes: Small, specialized benchmark focused on children's faces; likely limited public leaderboard activity and potential dataset-size constraints.
